added_failures_note: the reviewed run's manifest names no baseline_suite arm, so the machinery's base-vs-head delta reads no base log; its head arm (gate-head.log: 6 passed, 1 skipped) reports no FAILED or ERROR id, and added failures are a subset of head failures, so the run provably added none. The 1 failure in negative-control.log is the declared control, not a gate arm.

findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed run's manifest carries test_logs rather than the baseline_suite/after_suite pair the review store reads at annotate_review_of_run, so the base arm of the added-failure derivation resolves no log; the head arm gate-head.log reports 6 passed 1 skipped with no FAILED or ERROR id, which bounds added failures at zero, but the designed delta is not measurable from this manifest.

follow-on: _UNREACHABLE_MARKERS classifies "unauthorized" and "authentication required" as LayerRegistryUnreachable, so an expired or missing GHCR token makes the availability gate skip the layer set cleanly rather than fail, and a credential fault is indistinguishable from a network outage (plan s1 assumes a token is needed).

follow-on: the gate fetches only the analytic layer; the six ITER layer digests are asserted only as well-formed hex by test_the_recorded_digests_are_well_formed, so a transcription error in them would pass the gate. I verified all eight digests and sizes against the live v0.0.14 registry manifest and they are correct, so this is non-blocking, but the gate does not test it.

follow-on: test_unreachable_registry_yields_a_clean_skip drives fetch_layer with a mocked runner that is always unreachable, so the test can only ever skip and contributes no failure signal; the head arm's "1 skipped" is this arm, not evidence that the live registry was unreachable (the analytic fetch in the same arm reached it).

justifications.durability: the digest-mismatch refusal (test_altered_manifest_digest_refuses_the_layer, reproduced as the declared control) and the publish-then-reuse path are genuine guards over the store's atomic no-clobber publication; _publish_layer re-derives the store primitives correctly but omits the post-publish root-identity re-checks that materialize_machine_artifact performs (pinned_root_path, visible_root_matches_descriptor).
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the head arm (6 passed, 1 skipped, EXIT=0) and the declared negative control (1 failed, 5 passed, 1 skipped, EXIT=1) at the reviewed head, and independently fetched the v0.0.14 registry manifest and confirmed all eight pinned layer digests and sizes match; the gaps are that the reviewed run recorded no baseline_suite/after_suite arm so the base side of the added-failure derivation reads no log, and the gate fetches only the analytic layer.
justifications.fit: layer_fetch.py follows the surrounding module idiom, carries no plan, sprint or version label, and its error vocabulary (LayerFetchError with LayerRegistryUnreachable and LayerDigestMismatch subclassing it) is coherent; the import of both the content_store module and a long explicit name list is mildly redundant.
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/database/layer_fetch.py:88 fetch_layer addresses the layer by digest only (reference = registry@<digest> at line 116), refuses mismatched bytes in verify_layer_digest (line 74) and publishes into the content store, exactly as s3 prescribes, and tests/data-manifest.json gains exactly the s3 case records.
justifications.reuse: layer_fetch reuses the content store's file_content_identity, verify_directory_files and publication primitives rather than re-implementing hashing or the atomics, as s3 intends for the store's second consumer, but it repeats the ~40-line publication orchestration that machine_artifact.materialize_machine_artifact also codes because the store exposes no single generic publisher.
justifications.scope_discipline: the whole diff is four paths, each inside the manifest's declared write paths; no out-of-scope file is touched and no figure is required for this rung.
